purpose: Nisoldipine is used to treat high blood pressure, also called hypertension. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps lower your risk of having a stroke, heart attack, or kidney problems. Your doctor may prescribe this alone or along with other blood pressure medicines.
how_it_works: Your blood vessels have tiny channels that let calcium in, which causes the vessels to tighten and squeeze. Nisoldipine blocks those calcium channels so your blood vessels can relax and open up wider. When your vessels are more relaxed, your heart does not have to work as hard and your blood pressure goes down.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include swelling in your ankles or feet, headache, flushing or feeling warm in your face, dizziness, and a fast or pounding heartbeat. These are usually mild and may improve as your body adjusts to the medicine.
warnings: Do not eat grapefruit or drink grapefruit juice while taking this medicine because it can cause too much of the drug to build up in your body and increase side effects. Tell your doctor if you have heart failure or liver problems before starting this medicine. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this could cause your blood pressure to spike. Let your doctor know about all other medicines you take, as some can interact with nisoldipine.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 17 mg taken by mouth once a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over time, up to a maximum of 34 mg per day, depending on how your body responds. Always swallow the tablet whole on an empty stomach or with a light, low-fat meal — do not crush, chew, or split it.
